answer: A device that connects through two independent networks, such as cellular data and a fixed broadband link, must show the same city from both, because the two paths are run by different companies, meeting at one vertex of trust. A signal arriving from a distant relay breaks the agreement, a marble office cannot lend its connection across a border, and an onyx cable in the wall cannot hide the mismatch, so a farm needs a local broadband presence for every fake location.
